content.title: About
content.content: Mayonnaise-type salad dressing is an emulsion of vegetable oil, eggs, vinegar or lemon juice, and seasonings. It has a creamy texture, mild flavor, and is used as a salad dressing, sandwich spread, and base for many other sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic mayonnaise was created in the 19th century in France, and similar emulsions have spread worldwide.
Egg yolks act as natural emulsifiers, binding oil and water together.
There are many variations: olive‑oil based, yogurt‑based, avocado‑based, and other plant‑based versions.
Mayonnaise-type dressing is often taught in culinary schools to demonstrate emulsion techniques.
In many countries it is considered a “universal sauce” and is found in almost every household fridge.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: When made with oils high in monounsaturated fats (e.g., olive oil), the dressing can help maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs provide vitamin B12, riboflavin, and biotin, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: The oil component supplies vitamin E, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Improves nutrient absorption
items.content: Fats aid the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) from other foods in the salad.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Provides calories that can be useful for people with high energy needs, such as athletes.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: The presence of eggs makes the dressing a potential allergen for individuals with egg allergy.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of the oil, the dressing is calorie‑dense and should be used in moderation.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Raw eggs may contain Salmonella; using pasteurized eggs or commercially prepared products reduces this risk.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Egg yolks contain cholesterol, which may be a concern for people with hypercholesterolemia.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use as a dressing for green or vegetable salads, as a spread for sandwiches, in dips for veggie sticks, or as a base for more complex sauces (e.g., with mustard or herbs).

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, it is usually good for 1–2 weeks. Discard if it develops off‑odors, color changes, or mold.
